predecessors.name: Majeerteen Sultanate
predecessors.text: the southern edge of the Majeerteen shape trimmed when Cliopatria begins Hobyo in 1880 (about 760 km2)

predecessors.name: Hiraab Imamate
predecessors.text: central Somalia; the page lists the Hiraab Imamate as a predecessor without naming land

successors.name: Italian Africa
successors.text: Hobyo without the eastern Ethiopian part, integrated 'of Italian Somaliland in 1927' after the Campaign of the Sultanates

ledger.x: 1878: Yusuf Ali Kenadid founds the Sultanate of Hobyo in central Somalia.
1878: a southern strip of the Majeerteen shape goes to Hobyo (about 760 km2).
8 February 1889: Hobyo becomes an Italian protectorate.
1890: Cliopatria's shape loses about 27,000 km2 on the south-west (134,617 - 107,741 = 26,876 km2) (45.96-49.48E, 3.4-7.64N), where its Italian Africa row begins.

1900: the part of Hobyo's shape in eastern Ethiopia (91 H3 res-5 cells, about 23,000 km2) passes to the Ethiopian Empire, whose Cliopatria shape reaches 47.9 E from 1900 (the Ogaden occupied from 1891 per the ethiopian-empire dossier).
1 October 1925: Italian columns enter Hobyo and depose the sultan.
October 1925: the Sultanate of Hobyo ends with the deposition of Sultan Ali Yusuf Kenadid.

wars.name: Campaign of the Sultanates
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Hobyo is occupied 'completely within a few weeks' from 1 October 1925 and its ruler deposed; Omar Samatar's revolt takes El Buur (9 November 1925) and is crushed by 26 December 1925; the sultanate is integrated into Italian Somaliland.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the 1889 treaty fixes no frontier on the page; the borders are Cliopatria's approximations.
